newsitem.title: BULGARIA: National Bank of Greece opens Bulgaria branch.
newsitem.headline: National Bank of Greece opens Bulgaria branch.

text.p: Greece's largest commercial bank National Bank of Greece opened a branch in Bulgaria on Thursday to service increasing business links between the two countries.

"The main mission of the branch will be to work with the corporate clients of the bank who have invested or are ready to invest in the Bulgarian market," NBG governor Theodore Karatzas told a news conference.
The branch, licensed by the Bulgarian National Bank in 1995, aims to gradually build up its Bulgarian client base and offer retail services to Bulgarians as well, he added.

Besides Sofia, the NBG has branches in Tirana and Bucharest and plans to set up operations in Belgrade and Skopje as part of its Balkan expansion stragegy. NBG's assets exceed $33 billion. The bank has 83 units located in 14 countries.

Some 900 Greek joint ventures and representative offices now operate in Bulgaria, Greece's northern Balkan neighbour. Trade turnover between the two countries amounted to around $200 million last year.
Three Greek banks have already set up branches in Bulgaria in the past few years -- Egnatia Bank, Ionian and Xios Bank.
Registered Greek investment in Bulgaria amounts to only $55 million but officials said the real figure was probably over $100 million. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
